scope: Published Home only. No writes during this audit. Prior unpublished changes are not acceptance evidence.

rows.text: I’m Lainey, a rider and working student. I built RingStatus to keep horses, preparation, rides, and people organized through a day that keeps changing.
I need useful answers, not to get buried in notifications I can’t use. RingStatus sorts through changes for what matters. I use it with my team, see what helps, and keep adjusting
There’s getting everything to the show, caring for the horses, preparing for our classes, and keeping the team updated on progress. I need a plan that accounts for all of it.
Tap below to see how I keep up when things change.
Getting the horses and tack to a show takes planning, whether it’s nearby or hours away. I need to know what each horse needs, what’s packed, what’s still missing, and what I need
When the day changes, our plan needs to keep up.
As soon as the day starts, it feels like the plan already needs adjusting. Erasing the whiteboard in the barn doesn’t help me when I’m at Pony Island. RingStatus helps me work thro
Tap below to see how I keep up when things change.
The horses and their matching tack need to arrive together so we can get everything where it belongs and start horse care. As we unload, I need to know what’s missing or broken so
Now the team needs to know.
Once I update the plan, I need the people affected to know what changed and what they need to do. RINGSTATUS helps get each person the part that matters to them.
I’m really proud of the two-way SMS. It’s super helpful for getting exactly what I need without scrolling through my group chats and notifications.
I’m really proud of the two-way SMS. It’s super helpful for getting exactly what I need without scrolling through my group chats and notifications.
I see what works. And what doesn’t.
I’m riding, doing prep, and using RingStatus with my team. I see what helps, what gets ignored, and what’s still missing. Then I make adjustments and try again tomorrow.
My dad calls it ‘eating my own dog food’—whatever that means.
My dad calls it ‘eating my own dog food’—whatever that means.

It’s no secret—
show days are long.

My horse and I both ride better when I’m less stressed.
